identity.real_world_identity_notes: Secondary model history describes six-speed sequential hardware and a 2005 paddle-shift conversion. AMS2 shows both paddles and a cockpit lever, but the modeled driver retains both hands on the wheel through replay shifts, supporting paddle actuation for this representation.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a GT/Formula rim with an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with automatic cut; clutch-free downshifts were accepted with automatic throttle blip.

Both paddles and a cockpit sequential lever are visible, but exterior replay animation showed no driver hand leaving the wheel during shifts; paddle actuation is therefore the reviewed modeled control.
A future animation or cockpit-behavior change can falsify and trigger review of this actuation choice.
'Dallara SP1 - Low Downforce' inherits these verified base controls as an approved aero-package assumption and was not separately live-tested.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Standing-start clutch, six gears, automatic cut and blip, and GT/Formula display rim were directly observed.
Paddle actuation is based on visible paddles plus replay animation retaining both hands on the wheel; a cockpit lever is also present.
'Dallara SP1 - Low Downforce' is an exact observed identity inheriting the verified base controls; that aero configuration was not separately live-tested.

confidence.basis: Exact simulator identity and shift behavior were directly tested. Paddle actuation is supported by visible hardware, period secondary context, and modeled replay animation, with the visible lever explicitly retained as a review caveat.

claims.basis: Official release context and exact live CarModel/class observation establish the simulated identity.
Provisional historical context and direct exercise agree on six-speed sequential hardware.
Visible paddles, a period paddle-conversion context, and replay animation retaining both hands on the wheel support paddle actuation despite the additional cockpit lever.
Direct current-game tests and cockpit inspection establish technique and wheel category.

notes: 'Dallara SP1 - Low Downforce' is an exact approved alias whose controls are inherited from the verified base; it has not been separately live-tested.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "prototype", a value that named a racing category rather than a rim outline. That value is retired: the rims it covered are the same closed form, flattened at both the top and the bottom, that the project now records as "gt-style". The shape was remapped by definition and the rim was not observed again.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
